issues: length: §7 claims 'Hard ceiling 66 turns of the handle, even if not one dial ever moves,' derived from 40 gears + 6 hubs + 16 tokens = 62 build/pull actions plus one closing round. But §4 states every turn cranks regardless of action ('Step 2 — Crank... Then the turn passes to the left' happens after any of the four actions), and §5d says 'Re-dock is free. It costs only your turn' with no supply limit. Since Ending 2 only fires when a FULL round has zero builds/pulls/tokens spent, any single player occasionally building while others re-dock keeps that round 'active' indefinitely — free re-dock turns still crank the handle but aren't bounded by the 62-action budget. The 66-turn figure bounds build/pull actions, not total cranks/turns; disposition clarify (reword the ceiling claim to describe the build/pull budget, not total handle-turns).

length: the per-turn legality check as written — compute (my teeth + their teeth)÷2, check straight or against the 6-entry Pythagorean slant table (24 mirrored offsets), then verify the new gear isn't closer than its mesh number to EVERY other gear already on the plate ('No two gears may ever sit closer than their mesh number... if it does not drop in and spin freely, it is not a legal placement'), plus ring-parity jam checks — is materially heavier than a typical light-game turn, and grows each turn as more gears (up to 12–18 per §7's own estimate) accumulate on the board. §7's 'Expect 30 to 40 turns of the handle, which is 25 to 40 minutes including the teach' against target_minutes=30 assumes each decision is fast; the text gives no shortcut or aid (e.g. a printed distance card) to keep foul-checking fast as the board fills. disposition: clarify (only a reading-level concern about unsupported time claims — real per-turn timing needs a playout, not asserted here).

consistency: idea.json direction.weight is 'light', but rules.md's actual rules-count and interlocking edge cases (parity/mesh counting, Pythagorean slant table, planetary hub reveal-by-cranking, ring-closure jam rules, a 4-step tiebreak chain, and a dozen-plus §9 rulings) read closer to a medium-weight ruleset than a light one. disposition: clarify (labeling/calibration, not a mechanic defect).
